domain: flood warning operations / agency hazard-warning escalation
prediction_question: For a Flood Alert (or pre-2010 Flood Watch) issued by the Environment Agency for a target alert area P on day D, will any of the Flood Warning Areas whose register 'parent' is P receive a Flood Warning or Severe Flood Warning message during days D+1 through D+7, given only the warning-message history for P and its child areas through day D, the register attributes of P and its children, and the calendar?
prediction_time: Day-grain: the day D on which the alert message was issued. The dataset's DATE column carries no time-of-day (measured: 0 of 85,982 dated rows), so the prediction instant is the alert's issue day and the label window starts at D+1 because a same-day child warning cannot be ordered against the alert (46.9% of [D,D+7]-window positives were same-day). Features must be knowable by end of day D: message history through D (inclusive), register attributes (current-vintage snapshot, measured static in practice), and calendar.
target_definition: Binary label: 1 if any warning-level message (TYPE 'flood warning', 'severe flood warning', or their 'update' variants, case-normalised) for any warning area W with register parent(W) == P has issue date in [D+1, D+7]; else 0. Source columns: DATE, CODE, TYPE in the Historic Flood Warnings ODS joined to fws_tacode->parent in the Flood Warning Areas register (WFS, properties-only). Alert events eligible only when P has at least one child warning area (53,048 of 62,897 alert-level messages).

split_strategy: Temporal, one row per eligible alert event: train 2006-2019, eval 2020-2022, holdout 2023-2026 Q2 (file ends 2026-06-30). Measured at label window [D+1,D+7]: train 28,864 events / 3,638 positives (12.60%); eval 9,623 / 1,560 (16.21%); holdout 14,561 / 2,408 (16.54%). Positives occur in every year 2006-2026. Positives cluster by storm: 458 distinct year-weeks carry at least one positive (top week 2020-W7, Storms Ciara/Dennis, 324 same-window positives at the [D,D+7] definition). Report per-year metrics: a reporting-system migration in April 2017 (Floodline Warnings Direct -> Flood Warning System, per the EA's dataset description) is a candidate structural break.

measurements.source_rows: 85,982 dated message rows (85,993 data rows incl. 11 repeated header rows in the ODS), 2006-01-26 to 2026-06-25

code_coverage.note: unmatched codes are retired/renamed historic target areas; the register is a current-vintage snapshot and the EA does not publish historical register vintages, so historic parent linkage is unverifiable - a recorded assumption, not a reconstruction

clustering_D1_D7.note: storm clustering is real (top weeks: 2020-W7, 2024-W1, 2012-W47, 2020-W6, 2023-W52, 2014-W1); cluster-robust intervals required at qualification

persistence_probe.definition: single-rule baseline: a child warning occurred in the previous 7 days before D
persistence_probe.note: persistence is a weak single rule, not a dominant level - unlike nhs-ae-four-hour-decline; the full persistence/calendar/model triad is measured at qualification

extraction_cost.registers_wfs: 9 requests, 1,320,726 bytes, 3.8 s wall clock (coordinator-class machine, properties-only)
extraction_cost.parse_and_measure: in-memory parse of 85,993-row ODS plus full parent-linked label measurement: seconds on the coordinator
extraction_cost.note: the whole panel fits on the coordinator; construction needs no bulk worker download

data_quirks: TYPE values are case-inconsistent ('Flood alert' 3,011 / 'flood alert' 43,335 variants etc.); normalise before use
pre-2010 alert-level messages are named 'Flood Watch'
DATE column is day-grain despite documentation saying 'date and time' (measured: 0 of 85,982 rows carry a time)
removals ('warning no longer in force') are NOT in this dataset, so warning durations are unobservable; the label avoids durations by construction
the file is delivered as an ODS spreadsheet inside a ZIP, not CSV - parsing requires ODS content.xml handling

same-code alert->warning escalation is almost nonexistent (29 events in 20 years): escalation is a parent->child relation across two registers, not a same-code sequence - this is why the 'parent' attribute is the load-bearing discovery

prior_art: GFF coastal inundation benchmark (arXiv:2409.18591); Iowa flood-forecast DNN dataset (arXiv:1902.02308); HaorFloodAlert (arXiv:2605.20167); flood-related 112-call ML (NHESS 26:3943, 2026)
novelty_check.theirs: The publisher ships the raw event log (quarterly ODS), the two area registers (WFS), a live 3-day flood-risk forecast in the flood-monitoring API, and river-level telemetry (hydrology API). Research prior art is sensor-side: river-stage/inundation forecasting benchmarks (Iowa DNN arXiv:1902.02308, GFF arXiv:2409.18591, HaorFloodAlert arXiv:2605.20167, Wupper QML arXiv:2407.01001) and flood-related emergency-call prediction (NHESS 26:3943).
novelty_check.ours: First ML-ready dataset of an agency warning-escalation decision: parent-linked Flood Alert -> child Flood Warning within 7 days, on 53k real events over 20 years, with history-only features and temporal splits. Neither the label (a human operational decision, not a sensor value) nor the join (register 'parent' attribute) existed in any prior dataset.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
